name: Site purchasing: requisition to delivery at a remote underground gold mine
summary: Buyers at the mine turn approved purchase requisitions from maintenance, the warehouse, shutdown planners and capital projects into purchase orders, get quotes for larger or unusual items, route orders over their limit for approval, and then chase suppliers and freight until the goods reach a site about an hour's drive from the nearest town. Most of the elapsed time is supplier lead time and freight, but buyer queues, unclear requisitions, slow quotes and approval waits add days. Emergency breakdown parts jump the queue and are often collected by a site driver, and a winter highway closure can hold freight for a day or more.

baseline.org_archetype: A single-mine Canadian gold producer with about 280 people at a remote northern Ontario site, a mid-market ERP with purchasing and inventory modules, and a small site supply team under the site controller.
baseline.notes: Describes 2019-2022 practice: requisitions and POs in the ERP, quotes and supplier contact by email and phone, PO PDFs emailed to suppliers, freight consolidated through a carrier from southern and northeastern Ontario.

trigger: An approved purchase requisition (stock replenishment, maintenance work order part, shutdown scope item or capital item) lands in the buyers' ERP queue.
end_state: The goods are at site, the buyer has confirmed the delivery against the warehouse receipt and the PO is ready for invoice matching; or the requisition is cancelled.

volume.seasonality: Higher before planned mill and hoist shutdowns and in late summer and autumn when consumables and winter stock are built up before freeze-up; lower in the December holiday weeks.

evidence.note: Organisation file process_map volume (purchase-lines driver). Cross-checked against spend scale: 2021 guidance of C$900-1,000 per oz operating cost on about 100,000 oz plus C$45-53 million capital (wdo-guidance) gives roughly C$100 million a year of external spend, consistent with about 6,000 POs a year averaging tens of thousands of dollars once contractor spend is included.
Copied from the organisation file process_map surge: quarterly mill and hoist shutdown scopes add a burst of orders and expediting in the two to three weeks before each shutdown.

systems.name: Mid-market ERP for finance, purchasing, inventory and fixed assets
Shared drives and document library (procedures, permits, drawings)
Maintenance management system (ERP maintenance module or standalone)
Incident, inspection and training records system
Leaky feeder radio and surface radio network

steps.name: Pick up requisition from the queue
steps.description: The buyer opens the ERP list of approved requisitions assigned to them, sorted by need date and priority, opens the next one and reads the lines, the requisitioner's notes and any attached drawing or part number cross-reference.

evidence.note: Buyer queue of a few hours to two days for routine requisitions; emergency requisitions are phoned in and picked up at once. Estimate from common site practice.

steps.name: Check requisition completeness
steps.description: The buyer checks that each line has a usable part number or description, quantity, unit, cost code or work order, need date and an approver within limit. They compare the part against the item master and previous POs to spot duplicates of an open order.

error.defect_description: Duplicate of an open order or wrong unit of measure not spotted.

next.condition: missing part number, cost code or specification

evidence.note: Share of incomplete requisitions is an estimate; vague descriptions and missing cost codes are the usual causes at sites where maintenance planners raise requisitions under time pressure.

steps.name: Clarify requisition with requisitioner
steps.description: The buyer emails or radios the requisitioner, usually a maintenance planner, asking for the OEM part number, a photo of the nameplate, the cost code or a clearer specification. The planner looks it up in the maintenance system or asks the mechanic and edits the requisition.

evidence.note: Reply waits depend on the planner being on site and on the mechanic who knows the machine being on shift; one day is typical.

steps.name: Check stock, contracts and suppliers
steps.description: The buyer checks whether the item is stocked at site or on order, whether a blanket order or price agreement covers it, and who supplied it last and at what price. They decide whether the order can go straight to a known supplier or needs quotes under the purchasing policy.

next.condition: blanket order, price agreement, sole source or emergency order
new hazardous product not yet approved for site

evidence.note: The posting sets three quotes for items over C$500; this file assumes about a third of POs need quotes because blanket orders and contract pricing cover most repeat consumables (tier C share).

steps.name: Review safety data sheet for new hazardous product
steps.description: Before a chemical, lubricant or other hazardous product is bought for the first time, the safety coordinator reviews the supplier's safety data sheet, checks it against site restrictions underground and in the mill, and approves it into the site product list with any handling conditions.

control.basis: WHMIS 2015 requirement for current safety data sheets and site new-chemical approval procedure

evidence.note: Common mine practice under WHMIS: a safety data sheet must be available for hazardous products in the workplace; site new-product approval is a policy step. Not checked against the regulation text.

steps.name: Prepare and send request for quotation
steps.description: The buyer writes a request for quotation with the specification, quantity, need date, delivery to site terms and any certification needed, and emails it to three suppliers from the approved list.

evidence.note: Both describe preparing RFQs or inviting tenders and reviewing quotations.

steps.name: Suppliers return quotes
steps.description: Suppliers price the request, check stock and lead time, and email back quotes. Distributors in Sudbury, Sault Ste. Marie and Toronto answer within days; OEM and fabricated items take longer.

evidence.note: Quote turnaround of one to eight days is an estimate for industrial distributors and OEM dealers serving northern Ontario mines.

steps.name: Chase late quotes
steps.description: The buyer phones or emails suppliers that have not quoted, agrees a new date or decides to go ahead with two quotes and notes the reason on the requisition.

evidence.note: Estimate.

steps.name: Evaluate quotes
steps.description: The buyer puts the quotes side by side in a spreadsheet: unit price, freight to site, lead time, warranty and whether the item meets the specification. They pick the lowest total cost that meets the need date, or send technical alternatives to the requisitioner.

error.defect_description: Freight or lead time misread, so the cheapest quote misses the need date.

next.condition: technical alternative or engineered item needs requisitioner review

evidence.note: Posting: analyse RFQ results, negotiate and select on lowest total cost of ownership.

steps.name: Technical review of quotes by requisitioner
steps.description: The maintenance planner, sometimes with the maintenance supervisor, checks that the quoted alternative part fits the machine, compares data sheets and replies to the buyer with an accept or reject.

evidence.note: Estimate.

steps.name: Create purchase order in the ERP
steps.description: The buyer converts the requisition to a PO in the ERP, selects the supplier, enters prices, freight terms, delivery address and need date, checks the cost code or work order on each line and saves it for approval.

error.defect_description: Wrong price, unit of measure or cost code keyed on a line.

evidence.note: Posting: issue purchase orders and keep the ERP up to date.

steps.name: ERP routes PO by approval limit
steps.description: The ERP compares the PO value with the delegation of authority and either releases it on the buyer's own limit or puts it in the approver's queue and emails them.

control.basis: Delegation of financial authority approved by the board

evidence.note: Share of POs above a buyer limit of about C$10,000 is an estimate from typical mine spend profiles.

steps.name: Supply chain supervisor approves PO
steps.description: The supply chain supervisor opens the PO, checks the supplier, price against the quote file and whether competitive quotes were obtained, and approves it or returns it with a question.

control.basis: Delegation of financial authority: PO above buyer limit approved by someone other than the buyer

evidence.note: Estimate.

steps.name: Site controller checks budget and capital code
steps.description: For large POs the site controller checks that the spend is in the approved budget or an approved capital project, that the capital or operating code is right, and adds a note for the general manager.

control.basis: Capital expenditure policy and site budget control

evidence.note: Estimate; common control at single-mine companies where capital is tracked against board-approved projects.

steps.name: General manager approves PO
steps.description: The general manager reviews the large PO with the controller's note and approves it in the ERP, or forwards it to head office when it is above site authority.

control.basis: Delegation of financial authority approved by the board

evidence.note: Estimate.

steps.name: Chief operating officer approves PO
steps.description: The chief operating officer in Toronto reviews the PO and supporting quote comparison, sometimes calls the general manager, and approves it.

control.basis: Delegation of financial authority approved by the board

evidence.note: Estimate.

steps.name: Send PO to supplier
steps.description: The buyer prints the released PO to PDF and emails it to the supplier, or phones emergency orders through and sends the PO afterwards, asking for an acknowledgement with a ship date.

evidence.note: Estimate.

steps.name: Supplier acknowledges order
steps.description: The supplier confirms price, quantity and ship date, or replies with a price change, a back order or a substitute part.

evidence.note: Estimate.

steps.name: Issue PO change order
steps.description: The buyer amends the PO for the new price, date or substitute part, checks with the requisitioner when the date no longer meets the need, and sends the revised PO.

error.defect_description: Revised price not updated on the PO, causing an invoice mismatch later.

evidence.note: Posting lists issuing change orders.

steps.name: Expedite and track the order
steps.description: The buyer works the open-order report: past-due lines, critical spares and shutdown items. They call the supplier for ship dates and tracking numbers and tell the requisitioner when a date slips.

next.condition: order shipped or ready for pickup

evidence.note: Posting: expedite past-due and rush orders and follow up with end users. Time per PO is an estimate.

steps.name: Book freight to site
steps.description: The buyer arranges for the shipment to go through the site's consolidating carrier or warehouse in town, books a courier or hot-shot for urgent items, and adds the freight cost to the PO when it is charged separately.

evidence.note: Estimate; consolidated freight to remote sites through a carrier is common practice.

steps.name: Drive to collect an emergency part
steps.description: A warehouse attendant signs out the site pickup truck and drives to the nearest town, bus depot or airport to collect a breakdown part that a courier has brought north, then drives back to site.

evidence.note: A round trip of two to seven hours to town or the regional airport is an estimate from the site's distance to town in the organisation file; the wait is for a free driver and truck.

steps.name: Goods in transit to site
steps.description: The supplier ships and the carrier brings the goods north, usually on a scheduled consolidated run to site; back orders and long-lead items stretch this wait.

evidence.note: Lead time plus freight of two days to five weeks is an estimate for distributor stock and OEM parts shipped to northern Ontario.

steps.name: Freight held by highway closure
steps.description: Winter storms or collisions close the highway to site and the carrier holds the load in town until it reopens; the buyer updates the requisitioner on the new arrival.

evidence.note: Winter highway closures in northern Ontario are common knowledge; frequency and duration are estimates.

steps.name: Confirm delivery and close expediting
steps.description: The buyer checks the warehouse receipt against the PO, quantity and part number, clears the line from the open-order report and tells the requisitioner the item is in stores.

evidence.note: Estimate.

steps.name: Arrange return or replacement
steps.description: For a wrong, short or damaged shipment the buyer contacts the supplier, gets a return authorisation, arranges freight back and has the replacement shipped, and notes the claim for the accounts payable team.

evidence.note: Estimate.

exceptions.name: Incomplete requisition
exceptions.description: Missing part number, cost code or specification sends the requisition back to the planner.

exceptions.name: Emergency breakdown part
exceptions.description: A part for a down machine is phoned through, shipped by courier or hot-shot, and collected by a site driver.

exceptions.name: Large PO approval chain
exceptions.description: POs above C$50,000 go through the supply supervisor, site controller and general manager, and occasionally the COO.

exceptions.name: Weather hold on freight
exceptions.description: Highway closure holds a load in town.

exceptions.name: Wrong or damaged delivery
exceptions.description: Return and replacement restart the transit wait.

benchmarks.unit: calendar days from approved requisition to goods confirmed at site
benchmarks.population: Remote Canadian underground mine buying from Ontario distributors and OEMs, 2019-2022

evidence.note: Author's estimate: two to four days to place a PO plus one to two weeks of supplier lead time and freight; long-lead OEM parts drive the 90th percentile. APQC requisition-to-PO pages could not be opened.

benchmarks.unit: CAD per item above which three quotes are required
benchmarks.population: One Ontario gold operation's buyer posting

evidence.note: Thresholds differ by company; used only to describe the policy step.

pain_points.description: Two buyers carry about 500 POs a month plus expediting, so routine requisitions wait in the queue while emergencies are handled.

evidence.note: Follows from the organisation file headcount and volume and the touch times in this file.

pain_points.description: Vague requisitions (no OEM part number or cost code) bounce between buyer and planner.

evidence.note: Estimate from common practice.

pain_points.description: Approval of large POs waits on managers who are underground, on rotation or in Toronto.

evidence.note: Estimate.

pain_points.description: Long freight legs and winter road closures make expediting a large share of buyer time.

evidence.note: Expediting past-due and rush orders is a listed buyer duty.

sources.title: Buyer, Porcupine operations (Timmins, Ontario) job posting
sources.supports: Buyer at an Ontario underground and open pit gold operation follows the procure-to-pay process, obtains three quotes for items over $500, issues purchase orders and change orders, expedites past-due and rush orders, follows up with end users, updates the ERP and resolves invoice issues with vendors; reports to the procurement and warehouse manager.

sources.title: NOC 2021 unit group 12102: Procurement and purchasing agents and officers
sources.supports: Purchasing agents invite tenders, consult suppliers and review quotations, negotiate terms, award or recommend contracts, establish delivery schedules, monitor progress and contact suppliers to resolve problems.

sources.title: Wesdome Announces 2020 Fourth Quarter and Full Year Production Results; Provides 2021 Guidance
sources.supports: Eagle River complex 2021 guidance: 92,000-105,000 oz, operating cost C$900-1,000 per oz, AISC C$1,300-1,450 per oz, sustaining capital C$23-27 million and growth capital C$22-26 million; 2020 ore milled 236,297 t and production 90,278 oz.

assumptions: The process starts when a requisition is already approved by its department; requisition creation and departmental approval sit in the maintenance, warehouse and capital processes. Receiving and stores are the site-warehouse process; this file only covers the buyer's confirmation of the receipt.

Approval limits are assumed: buyer up to about C$10,000, supply chain supervisor up to C$50,000, general manager up to site authority (about C$250,000-500,000), COO above. Shares of POs in each band are estimates.

Staffing gap: the touch times (about 45 minutes of buyer time per PO on average) imply about 3.7 FTE of buyer work at 500 POs a month, against 2 buyers in the organisation file. The file keeps the estimated touch times rather than shrinking them to fit; the evidence on buyer duties (quotes, change orders, expediting, invoice issues) points to 3-4 purchasing staff, or a buyer plus an expediter, at this volume.

Shift patterns: buyers, the supply chain supervisor and the site controller are set to office_hours (weekday days) because the organisation file gives them no rotation; requests that arrive on Friday evening wait for Monday.
The site pickup truck is not in the organisation file's resource list and is added here with not_in_org_file.
Loaded costs are taken from the organisation file (wage times 1.30 for staff roles).

The simulated median of about 19 days is above the 14-day estimate in benchmarks because quote waits (s07), approval waits and the expediting cycle stack on top of transit; the 90th percentile (about 31 days) is below the 40-day estimate because very long OEM lead times are folded into the high end of one triangular wait. Both are within the range the estimate rests on, so the times were not forced to match.
Elapsed time is dominated by supplier lead time and freight (s23), which is outside the company's control; the simulated cycle covers requisition to delivery, not requisition to PO.
